newsitem.title: UK: Dlr gains point to independent strength-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Dlr gains point to independent strength-analysts.

text.p: The dollar's climb against the Swiss franc to its highest levels since August 1993 may be a sign of independent dollar strength, currency analysts said.
So far, dollar strength in Europe has been attributed first to yield factors and then to general weakness in Europe as EU members knuckle down to prepare for monetary union.
But dollar gains against the Swiss franc, the last of the major European currencies to succumb to dollar strength, are coinciding with new highs in the dollar's trade weighted index for this decade.
The Bank of England dollar trade weighted index tested a new high of 99.13 on Friday.
Dealers said the idea of the Swiss franc as a safe-haven against the perception of a soft euro had previously kept dollar/Swiss gains in check.

"The markets had been trading under the faulty assumption that the Swiss franc had decoupled from its European partners, so this move is not so surprising," said Peter von Maydell, currency economist at UBS in London.
The dollar's break above key resistance at 1.4930 against the Swiss franc on Thursday and then above 1.51 on Friday morning has dispelled the safe-haven idea.

"The dollar had been bumping up to the 1.49-area since early this year, but the safe-haven story seemed to hold it back," said a U.S. bank dealer. "It was astonishing that the Swiss franc refused to go down given its low rates and weak economy."
By 1140 GMT, the dollar stood at 1.5144/54 francs, down from nearly a four-year peak of 1.5176 earlier but up from late Thursday's European level of 1.5018/23.
The dollar/Swiss gain in early trade helped dollar/mark to test a fresh six-year peak of 1.8403.

But analysts said the market was showing caution at that level. The German central bank's two-week fixing of the repo within the four-week summer recess signalled it was prepared to act on runaway mark weakness.

"The Bundesbank is giving a signal by just providing one more fixed tender, now it wants to check the market reaction," said Klaus Kusber, currency analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson in Frankfurt. "But a switch to a variable is only likely if they see a long-term inflation threat from the weak mark."
At 1215 GMT, dollar/mark was trading at 1.8360/70, down from its earlier six-year high above 1.8403 but still above late Thursday's 1.8310/20 marks.
Analysts are still bullish on dollar/mark going even higher and are mindful that it will be the pace of mark declines rather than absolute levels dictating Bundesbank action.

Elsewhere, dollar/yen was steady above 116.00 after touching a near one-month high of 116.63 in earlier trade. Mark/yen was also steady above 63.00 yen but down from an earlier top just below 63.50 seen in morning trade.
